title: Bitcoin Could Be Entering a New Bull Market Despite Latest Sell-Off
summary: BloFin Research says Bitcoin's new bull market remains intact despite the latest sell-off, as historical data suggests its boom-and-bust cycles are weakening.
content:
Despite the market dip and liquidations over the past week, Bitcoin has seemingly entered a bull market, as the analysis of its 50-week moving average shows.

BloFin Research argues that Bitcoin's traditional four-year boom-and-bust cycle is gradually losing strength. Future rallies could deliver smaller gains, followed by shorter and less severe downturns.

The strongest evidence comes from Bitcoin's recovery above its 50-week moving average, a technical indicator that previously signaled bull-market transitions in 2015, 2019 and 2023.

Bitcoin reclaimed this level near $78,800 in September. It subsequently traded above $86,000 in early October.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin's MVRV ratio, which compares its current market value with the average price investors paid for their coins, moved above its annual average.

As of October 11, MVRV stood near 1.54, above its 365-day average of 1.44. This suggests the longer-term recovery remains intact despite recent selling.

It means Bitcoin's market strength is improving, a signal that has previously appeared during the early stages of bull markets.

BloFin's most significant finding concerns the declining severity of Bitcoin's market cycles.

Bitcoin fell approximately 53% from its October 2025 peak of $124,824 to $58,525 in June 2026.

Previous bear markets were considerably worse:

Bear market

Peak-to-trough decline

2013–2015

84.5%

2017–2018

83.8%

2021–2022

76.7%

2025–2026

53%

Bull-market gains have also narrowed. Bitcoin's trough-to-peak returns have declined from roughly 530 times in its earliest cycle to eight times in the most recent one.

If June remains the bottom, the latest bear market lasted approximately eight months, compared with 12–13 months historically.

BloFin Research attributes much of this change to longer-term ownership. In September, approximately 16.64 million BTC, or 83% of circulating supply, had remained unmoved for at least 155 days.

Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin ETFs held around 1.3 million BTC on October 2. Public companies owned another 1.29 million BTC.

Together, ETFs and corporate treasuries controlled approximately 13% of circulating Bitcoin.

However, last week's $679 million ETF outflow shows that institutional demand can still weaken sharply during market stress.

Bitcoin was trading around $83,000 on October 11, still above the September moving-average breakout level and well above its June low.

The four-year cycle also remains visible. Bitcoin peaked roughly 18 months after the April 2024 halving, consistent with historical patterns.

For traders, a sustained move below the current 50-week moving average would weaken the bullish signal. A break beneath $58,525 would challenge the proposed cycle bottom.

For now, Bitcoin's longer-term recovery indicators remain positive. The recent ETF withdrawals show why the transition toward a more stable market could still involve sharp corrections.

Read the Original story Bitcoin Could Be Entering a New Bull Market Despite Latest Sell-Off by BloFin Research at beincrypto.com

title: AI Price Prediction: Insights from Grok on Bitcoin’s Potential by Election Day
summary: Grok crunched Bitcoin's price structure, fund flows, and midterm election history to land on a specific target for November 3. Whether its forecast holds depends on two price zones every Bitcoin holder should know right now.
content:
Grok forecasts Bitcoin closes around $85,000 on November 3 midterm election day, just above its current $82,940 price.

Grok assigns a 30% chance Bitcoin exceeds $90,000 and a 25% chance it drops below $75,000 by election day.

Election results could swing Bitcoin 7% in either direction within a week, with congressional control influencing key crypto legislation.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Grok, the AI chatbot developed by xAI, expects that Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) could close around $85,000 on November 3, 2026, the day of the U.S. midterm elections. This forecast is only slightly above Bitcoin's current price of about $82,940, as of October 11.

Bitcoin has dipped 2.7% in the past week but gained 7.4% over the last month. In just two weeks, it hit a high of $87,249 on October 2, then fell to $80,000 on October 8. So, how did Grok arrive at the $85,000 target, and how much weight should Bitcoin holders give it?

Before we asked our question, we gave Grok some relevant data. At the time, Bitcoin was trading at $83,007, roughly a year after it hit an all-time high of $126,080 on October 6, 2025. The lowest point since then was on June 30, when it fell to $57,717.

Since then, Bitcoin has made higher lows, suggesting each pullback has stopped above the last, with buyers stepping in around the mid-$70,000s in September and again at $80,000 on October 8. On that date, exchanges had to close $1.1 billion worth of leveraged positions—trades made with borrowed funds that exchanges close once losses eat through the trader's deposit.

------

Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.

That is exactly what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps answer. It covers what your retirement could actually cost, which income sources are worth using, and the withdrawal math that decides whether the money lasts. It is free today from Fisher Investments. Read More Here ›

------

We also shared information about Bitcoin funds. Spot Bitcoin funds, which directly hold Bitcoin for investors who buy shares through brokerage accounts, have a total of $105.8 billion in assets. These funds saw a $731 million outflow on October 7 and 8, but investors added $21 million on October 9.

Finally, we included historical election data, noting that Bitcoin fell about 20% in the month leading up to the 2022 midterms, largely due to the collapse of a major crypto exchange, and dropped about 7% in the four weeks before the 2018 midterms.

Grok believes Bitcoin is consolidating, trading in a relatively narrow range while maintaining its pattern of higher lows. It also considered the short-term holder cost basis—the average price recent buyers paid—which Grok assessed at the low-to-mid $70,000s. This price point matters because traders often watch it, knowing newer buyers might sell if prices fall below what they paid.

According to Grok, the price structure remains positive as long as Bitcoin stays above this support zone. It identified resistance, where selling typically occurs, in the mid-to-high $80,000s. Grok's main scenario suggests a slow upward trend, tempered by caution ahead of the elections and the historical trend of weak fourth quarters during midterm years. However, it noted the uncertainty of this trend, as past cycle bottoms and the 2022 exchange failure complicate the picture.

Volatility is a key reason Grok maintains its close-to-current price forecast. Options traders gauge implied volatility, or expected price movement, using contracts that let them buy or sell in the future at a set price. Grok noted a reading in the mid-30s, signifying a probable swing of around 8% to 9% in the three weeks before the elections.

Grok provided an 80% confidence range for Bitcoin's price on November 3, estimating it between $72,000 and $97,000. The lower end of this range reflects a possible test of short-term holder support, while the upper end suggests a potential breakout above recent highs.

Additionally, Grok assigned a 30% chance of Bitcoin exceeding $90,000 on November 3, and a 25% chance of it dropping below $75,000. This assessment leans slightly to the upside, tempered by election-related uncertainties and recent fund outflows.

We inquired whether the election outcome could influence Bitcoin's price. Grok confirmed it could, expecting a potential price move of about 7% in either direction within a week after the election, depending on how the results align with investor expectations. Control of Congress can also affect key crypto legislation, such as the stalled CLARITY Act. Historically, Bitcoin's price reactions after elections have varied, though it often trends positively over more extended periods.

Grok formulated its forecasts based on the data we provided, without access to live buy and sell orders on exchanges. The model also independently calculated the probabilities rather than reading them from any market.

We consider Grok's $85,000 estimate a reasonable midpoint for this three-week forecast, mainly because volatility metrics suggest limited room for significant movement in either direction. Bitcoin holders should watch two key areas: a close above Grok's resistance in the mid-to-high $80,000s could validate its more optimistic scenarios, while a drop below the low-to-mid $70,000s could bring the $72,000 lower boundary into play.

Monitoring fund flows provides an additional gauge. After the $731 million outflow from Bitcoin funds on October 7 and 8, steady inflows could help support the upward move Grok described. Ultimately, Bitcoin's price on November 3 will put Grok's model to the test.

title: Bitcoin and ethereum prices today, Friday, October 9, 2026: Bitcoin, ethereum open at lowest levels in about 3 weeks
summary: Bitcoin opened at $81,690.49 on Friday, October 9, 2026, down 1.9% from Thursday's open. As of 7:20 a.m. ET this morning, the price of bitcoin jumped to $82,468.42. Ethereum opened at $2,472.47, down 3.9% from Thursday's opening price. The price of ethereum moved up to $2,490.12 as of 7:20 a.m. ET.
content:
Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) opened at $81,690.49 on Friday, October 9, 2026 , down 1.9% from Thursday's open. As of 7:20 a.m. ET this morning, the price of bitcoin jumped to $82,468.42 .

Ethereum ( ETH-USD ) opened at $2,472.47 on Friday, October 9, 2026 , down 3.9% from Thursday's opening price. The price of ethereum moved up to $2,490.12 as of 7:20 a.m. ET.

Bitcoin and ethereum prices opened this morning at their lowest levels in about three weeks as crypto investors grapple with persistently high oil costs, expectations of rate increases this year and next, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East that seem to shift with each passing day.

Add to that laundry list the ongoing AI boom, and risk-based investments, like crypto, have many investors moving money to other, potentially safer opportunities:

Bitcoin price fell for a fourth consecutive day, briefly slipping below $81,000 before rebounding, as the total crypto market cap dropped below $2.8 trillion to a one-month low. The immediate question is whether BTC can withstand unstable spot Bitcoin ETF flows, forced selling, and a less favorable macro backdrop.

Keep reading: Bitcoin Price Briefly Reclaims $81,000 as Liquidations Top $1 Billion

The price of bitcoin this morning, Friday, October 9, 2026 , was down 1.9% compared to Thursday's opening price. Here's a look at how the opening bitcoin price has changed versus last week, month, and year:

One week ago: -3.7%

One month ago: +4.1%

One year ago: -33.8%

The all-time high for bitcoin was $126,198.07 on Oct. 6, 2025. The all-time low value for bitcoin was $0.04865 on July 14, 2010.

The price of ethereum this morning, Friday, October 9, 2026 , was 3.9% lower than Thursday's open. Here's a look at how the opening ethereum price has changed versus last week, month, and year:

One week ago: -8.6%

One month ago: -0.5%

One year ago: -45.4%

The all-time high for ethereum was $4,953.73 on Aug. 24, 2025. The all-time low value for ethereum was $0.4209 on Oct. 21, 2015.

Bitcoin, ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies are rapidly evolving. Follow the latest developments from Yahoo Finance and others here .

So, you put a little mad money into bitcoin a few years ago. Now, your crypto-fueled profit means you have a sweet nest egg to put toward a house.

But can you buy a house with crypto rather than using cash or a traditional mortgage loan? What are the roadblocks? And what about taxes?

President Trump wants the United States to be "the crypto capital of the world." In that spirit, in late June, Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) William J. Pulte ordered Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to "prepare their businesses to count cryptocurrency as an asset for a mortgage."

The FHFA supervises Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the government-sponsored companies that fund a major portion of the mortgage industry.

Pulte said the housing system "needs a massive upgrade," adding, "I want people who own cryptocurrency to be able to buy homes like everyone else. I believe cryptocurrency is an asset. I believe Americans should be able to use their crypto if they want to. It's time the housing system caught up."

This signals what could be a fundamental change to how cryptocurrency may be used to qualify for a mortgage.

title: Bitcoin rebounds above $83,000 after weekly slide as oil, yields and security fear
summary: Investing.com -- Bitcoin recovered on Saturday but remained on course for a weekly loss, as rising oil prices, higher U.S. Treasury yields and renewed cryptocurrency security concerns weighed on sentiment.
content:
Investing.com -- Bitcoin recovered on Saturday but remained on course for a weekly loss, as rising oil prices, higher U.S. Treasury yields and renewed cryptocurrency security concerns weighed on sentiment.

Before you buy NVIDIA: our AI model's stock picks are beating the market by 120%+. See the list now »

Bitcoin was trading at $83,025.4 by 14:23 ET (18:23 GMT), up 0.7% on the day, after moving between $82,537.7 and $83,164.1. The world's largest cryptocurrency had retreated from near $87,000 last Sunday, leaving it down around 3% over the past week.

Substantial spot exchange-traded fund outflows underscored continued uncertainty over institutional demand.

Rising energy prices, higher Treasury yields, concerns over AI-related hardware-wallet vulnerabilities and reports of a Ledger-linked cryptocurrency theft added to uncertainty around the first anniversary of the October 10 flash crash.

Bitcoin recorded 10 days in 2026 when its price moved at least three standard deviations from its recent trading pattern, exceeding the eight recorded throughout 2018, according to CoinDesk analysis, even as annualized volatility fell to 46% from 84% in 2018.

A separate CoinDesk Research analysis found that Bitcoin order-book depth within 1% of its price reached $11.7 million on October 7, about 75% above its level on crash day. Ether liquidity has also recovered, but dollar-denominated altcoin market depth has fallen by about a third since early 2025. Weekly spot trading volume remained nearly two-thirds below the $801 billion recorded during the crash week.

Not finding the right stocks? Our AI's list of investor-grade stock picks for October just dropped »

September's consumer price index and producer price index reports, due next week, will offer further clues on whether the Federal Reserve could resume raising interest rates. Markets expect rates to remain unchanged at the October 27-28 meeting, with a potential 25-basis-point increase in December.

Institutional demand has also weakened. SoSoValue data showed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of approximately $681.11 million across the five trading sessions from October 5 to October 9. Withdrawals reached $487.07 million on October 7 and $244.13 million on October 8, partly offset by inflows of $118.86 million on October 6 and $21.13 million on October 9.

Security concerns persisted after Ledger investigated reports of missing cryptocurrency linked to devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, which it asked to suspend sales and shipments. Investigators estimated losses of $86 million to $93.4 million, although Ledger has not confirmed the figures or cause. There is no confirmed evidence that its own systems were compromised.

Meanwhile, Strategy's NASDAQ-listed preferred shares, STRC, reached $99.71 on Friday, their highest since June. The shares carry a 12% annualized dividend, supported by the company's dollar reserves. A move above $100 could enable further preferred-share issuance to finance Bitcoin purchases.

Broader cryptocurrency prices were mostly higher. World No. 2 cryptocurrency Ether rose 1% to $2,509.39, while World No. 3 cryptocurrency XRP gained 1.1% to $1.4037.

Solana advanced 0.6% to $110.061, while BNB rose 1.4% to $749.80.

Cardano jumped 6.9% to $0.2535, while Dogecoin gained 1.7% to $0.086077.

Among meme coins, TRUMP rose 2.2% to $1.90, while Shiba Inu gained 1.4% to $0.00000547.

Simon Mugo contributed to this article.

Bitcoin was trading at $83,025.4 by 14:23 ET (18:23 GMT), up 0.7% on the day, after moving between $82,537.7 and $83,164.1. The world's largest cryptocurrency had retreated from near $87,000 last Sunday, leaving it down around 3% over the past week.

Substantial spot exchange-traded fund outflows underscored continued uncertainty over institutional demand.

Rising energy prices, higher Treasury yields, concerns over AI-related hardware-wallet vulnerabilities and reports of a Ledger-linked cryptocurrency theft added to uncertainty around the first anniversary of the October 10 flash crash.

Bitcoin recorded 10 days in 2026 when its price moved at least three standard deviations from its recent trading pattern, exceeding the eight recorded throughout 2018, according to CoinDesk analysis, even as annualized volatility fell to 46% from 84% in 2018.

A separate CoinDesk Research analysis found that Bitcoin order-book depth within 1% of its price reached $11.7 million on October 7, about 75% above its level on crash day. Ether liquidity has also recovered, but dollar-denominated altcoin market depth has fallen by about a third since early 2025. Weekly spot trading volume remained nearly two-thirds below the $801 billion recorded during the crash week.

September's consumer price index and producer price index reports, due next week, will offer further clues on whether the Federal Reserve could resume raising interest rates. Markets expect rates to remain unchanged at the October 27-28 meeting, with a potential 25-basis-point increase in December.

Institutional demand has also weakened. SoSoValue data showed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of approximately $681.11 million across the five trading sessions from October 5 to October 9. Withdrawals reached $487.07 million on October 7 and $244.13 million on October 8, partly offset by inflows of $118.86 million on October 6 and $21.13 million on October 9.

Solana advanced 0.6% to $110.061, while BNB rose 1.4% to $749.80.

Cardano jumped 6.9% to $0.2535, while Dogecoin gained 1.7% to $0.086077.

title: Bitcoin Rebounds After Rough Week, But Traders Are Pricing In More Downside
summary: Bitcoin bounced after dipping to around $80,000. Traders are placing increasingly high odds BTC slips further before October is over.
content:
The crypto markets are breathing today, with the total capitalization up 2.1% to $2.89 trillion on Friday. The bounce recovers only part of the damage, since the market stood above $3 trillion a week ago, when Bitcoin was pressing against its yearly high.

Despite the recovery, traders are still nervous. The Fear & Greed Index dropped to 56, a neutral reading, down from the 71 that put sentiment firmly in "greed" territory on October 2.

Wall Street is also nervous. Bitcoin ETFs alone shed $484.9 million on Wednesday, their worst day since June 25, and a further $244 million on Thursday, according to Decrypt's ETF tracker .

Bitcoin trades around $82,837 on Friday, up 1.38% on the day, after dipping to $80,427 on Thursday, its lowest level since early September.

The daily candle opened at $81,711 and has ranged between $81,553 and $83,443. On the four-hour chart, price still trades below the 50-period exponential moving average, so the short-term trend has not turned.

Myriad, a prediction market owned by Decrypt 's parent company Dastan, gives a 67% chance that Bitcoin trades at or below $80,000 at some point in October, with 40% odds for $77,500 and 24% for $75,000.

A separate weekly market put 49% odds on Bitcoin finishing the week above $87,500 so traders expect a month of price compression with some space for further downside.

The Average Directional Index, or ADX, which measures trend strength regardless of direction, reads 37.9 on the daily chart, well above the 25 level that confirms a real trend. The directional lines show buyers (DI+) above sellers (DI-), so the trend is still bullish even after the pullback.

The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, gauges buying pressure on a scale of 0 to 100, and its 51.2 reading is neutral, just like the Fear and Greed Index. This is worth checking out, because Bitcoin appears to be cooling down after an overbought phase.

Bitwise Europe's Luke Deans told Decrypt that the $83,000 zone combines the average ETF cost basis with the prior higher-high level, which makes it the first test for the bounce.

Reclaiming it would put the price zone at $84,433 in play, while the September high at $87,354.33 remains the ceiling bulls need a daily close above.

The world's largest cryptocurrency was trading at $83,062.8 as at 01:23 ET (05:23 GMT), having failed to recover its October 6, 2025, peak of $126,080.

The anniversary follows another volatile week in which Bitcoin fell to $80,308 before recovering towards $83,000, highlighting persistent concerns over leveraged trading.

On October 10, 2025, Bitcoin plunged from approximately $122,000 to $105,000 after President Donald Trump announced sweeping tariffs on Chinese imports.

The selloff triggered more than $19 billion in liquidations across cryptocurrency markets, affecting approximately 1.6 million trading accounts.

Analysts warn that the conditions behind the crash remain largely intact, particularly the widespread use of perpetual futures and heavily leveraged positions.

Mark Connors of Risk Dimensions said derivatives positioning continues to influence Bitcoin's short-term price movements, despite improvements in market transparency.

Recent positioning data suggests approximately $3.3 billion in Bitcoin short positions could face liquidation if prices climb towards $85,000, potentially accelerating any recovery.

Institutional demand has also weakened, with US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recording more than $700 million in outflows this week.

Despite the market's struggles, Bitwise Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan remains optimistic about Bitcoin's long-term prospects.

Hougan suggested Bitcoin's market capitalisation could eventually reach $30 trillion, drawing comparisons with gold's expansion following the introduction of exchange-traded funds.

The combination of institutional adoption and persistent leverage risks underscores Bitcoin's competing market forces.

While improved trading data may help investors identify crowded positions, analysts caution that another large-scale liquidation event remains possible.

For now, Bitcoin faces an immediate test around $85,000, with its longer-term recovery dependent on renewed demand and more stable market positioning.

title: Bitcoin Tests Average Buyer’s Break-Even As ETF Outflows Clash With Wall Street Buying
summary: Darkfost said the market was oscillating around the $80,500 line in a pattern resembling late 2025 and early 2026, with the level holding as support for now.
content:
Bitcoin traded almost flat on Saturday, hovering just above $82,900.

CryptoQuant Darkfost analyst described this level as the average holder's break-even point.

On Wall Street, Fidelity's FBTC bought $354.1 million of Bitcoin over 20 trading days while Morgan Stanley added 92 coins this week to reach 10,639 BTC.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded flat on Saturday, sitting just above the price at which the average holder was neither up nor down, as one analyst said the setup looked like a repeat of a pattern from late last year.

That line sat around $80,500, according to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost. It was the cost basis of all Bitcoin in circulation, weighted by how much money went into each purchase, so when the price hovered there, the market as a whole was roughly breaking even.

Darkfost said Bitcoin was oscillating around the break-even line in a pattern that resembled late 2025 and early 2026. A market sitting on that line created doubt, he said, which pushed investors to act. For now, it was holding as support.

Analyst Ted Pillows was watching slightly higher. A weekly close above $82,700 would mean buyers are in control, he said, and could open a move toward $87,000 to $88,000.

Bitcoin's price was trading at around $82,900, up by 0.3% at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it stayed at 'low' levels over the past day.

Two of the largest names on Wall Street have kept adding while the price has gone sideways. Fidelity's FBTC fund bought $354.1 million of Bitcoin over the past 20 trading days, according to Arkham. Its other crypto funds bought in the same window, taking in $66.6 million of Ethereum (ETH) and $18.2 million of Solana (SOL). Morgan Stanley (MS) also added about 92 coins this week through its MSBT fund, Arkham data showed, lifting its total to 10,639 BTC worth roughly $880 million.

Those two funds were buying even as the broader ETF category bled money this week. US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $487.07 million on Wednesday, and another $244.13 million on Thursday, according to SoSoValue data. A $21.13 million inflow on Friday recovered a fraction of it.

title: Weekly Wrap: Rising Treasury Yields Sink Bitcoin
summary: Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) is on track for a losing week as rising Treasury yields continue to pressure risk assets suc...
content:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) is on track for a losing week as rising Treasury yields continue to pressure risk assets such as stocks and crypto. In late trading on Oct. 9, Bitcoin's price was at $82,250 U.S., down nearly 5% over the past week. Digital assets have been under pressure as yields on U.S. government bonds steadily rise.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury has risen by 5.25% from 4.79% since Sept. 1. That's a big move in Treasury yields in a little over a month. At 5.25%, the yield on the 10-year Treasury is now at its highest level since April 2002. Higher yields offered by bonds attract investors, leading them to rotate capital out of riskier assets such as crypto.

So far in October, Bitcoin is down 1.50%, a sharp reversal from the 42% gain achieved in this year's third quarter. The decline to begin October is atypical for digital assets. October is usually the best month of the year for Bitcoin, producing an average increase of 18%. October has often been so strong for crypto that investors call the month "Uptober." But that does not appear to be the case so far this month.

Stacks Founder Warns Bitcoin Security Breach Could Hit Entire Crypto Market

Coinbase Targets Banks As Institutional Crypto Adoption Grows

60 Percent of Community Banks See Stablecoins as a Threat to Deposits, Lending

Crypto Heavyweights Back OKX at $25B Valuation

Here's what else happened in the crypto sector over the past week…

Outflows From Bitcoin ETFs Surge: The continued rise of U.S. Treasury yields is leading to an exodus of investor capital from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs). On Oct. 7, about a dozen U.S. spot ETFs saw net outflows of $487.1 million U.S., the most since June 25 of this year, according to data from SoSoValue. After seeing $2.65 billion U.S. of net inflows in September, capital has again begun to leave the Bitcoin funds. So far in October, the ETFs are down $165 million U.S.

Tom Lee Says Bitmine Will Stop ETH Purchases: The price of Ethereum fell 5% on news that crypto treasury firm Bitmine Immersion Technologies (NYSE: $BMNR) plans to stop buying the second-largest digital asset. Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said at a conference that the company will stop accumulating ETH once its holdings reach 5% of the token's circulating supply. Lee was adamant that Bitmine has set a hard ceiling on its accumulations of Ethereum, which is fast approaching the 5% target. Bitmine currently owns 6,016,414 ETH tokens, or slightly more than 4.9% of the 122.1 million circulating supply.

Robinhood Adds $25 Million Of Bitcoin To Its Balance Sheet: Online brokerage Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ: $HOOD) has added $25 million U.S. of Bitcoin to its balance sheet. The company, which offers stock and crypto trading through a popular app, said it added Bitcoin to its corporate balance sheet to demonstrate that it cares about the cryptocurrency ecosystem. Robinhood is one of several U.S. companies that is holding Bitcoin as a treasury asset. Other corporate holders of Bitcoin include electric vehicle maker Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA) and financial technology company Block (NYSE: $XYZ).

Strategy Adds 334 Bitcoin: Strategy (NASDAQ: $MSTR) slowed its pace of Bitcoin buying over the last week, adding 334 of the digital tokens to its holdings. The company led by Michael Saylor spent $28.7 million U.S. on its Bitcoin purchases over the past week, bringing its total holdings to 848,000 BTC with an average price of $75,441 U.S. The company also raised $15.7 million U.S. via the sale of common stock. Strategy's Bitcoin holdings are now worth $72.93 billion U.S.

NFL Calls Prediction Markets 'Gambling': The National Football League (NFL) has said that prediction markets are "gambling" and not "swaps" as companies such as Kalshi and Polymarket claim. The professional football league made the statement in a brief it filed related to a case that's before the U.S. Supreme Court. The NFL is supporting the State of New Jersey in its assertion that prediction markets are gambling and should be regulated alongside casinos and other gaming companies.

Thailand Allows Trading In Crypto ETFs: Thailand is opening its main stock exchange to Bitcoin and Ethereum (CRYPTO: $ETH) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) starting on Oct. 16. Bitcoin and Ethereum will be the only cryptocurrency ETFs available on Thailand's stock market during the initial rollout. Each crypto ETF must operate as a passive investment fund designed to track the spot price of Bitcoin or Ethereum.

Stripe Expands Stablecoin Cards To 100 Countries: Financial technology company Stripe says it plans to expand its stablecoin payment cards to more than 100 countries by year's end. Stripe said the expansion is part of its bet that digital dollars can become another way for consumers and businesses to make payments alongside traditional currencies. Stablecoin cards have emerged as a fast-growing part of the $300 billion U.S. market for digital dollars. About $1.2 billion U.S. of stablecoins were spent through cards in September of this year, triple the amount from a year earlier, according to Paymentscan.

Winklevoss Twins To Launch New Zcash ETF: Twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss are planning to launch a new Zcash (CRYPTO: $ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The ETF will hold ZEC directly. The new ETF proposes charging a 0.25% annual fee and will be listed on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "WINK." The fund still needs to be approved by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Crypto Job Postings Tripled In September: Cryptocurrency companies are ramping up their hiring as prices for digital assets rally and the "crypto winter" that began a year ago shows signs of ending. Crypto firms listed 1,241 job openings in September compared to 886 in August and 382 in July, according to data from crypto recruitment platform CryptoJobsList. The September total was more than double the 573 jobs posted in January of this year, which was the busiest month of the year until August.

Coinbase Targets Banks: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global (NASDAQ: $COIN) is targeting banks as institutional adoption of cryptocurrencies continues to grow. Coinbase is expanding its services for banks and other traditional financial firms as institutions continue to adopt Bitcoin and other crypto. Coinbase and other crypto firms are offering services such as custody, trading, financing, and settlement to leading banks around the world.

The company led by Michael Saylor spent $28.7 million U.S. on its Bitcoin purchases over the past week, bringing its total holdings to 848,000 BTC with an average price of $75,441 U.S. The company also raised $15.7 million U.S. via the sale of common stock. Strategy's Bitcoin holdings are now worth $72.93 billion U.S.

NFL Calls Prediction Markets 'Gambling': The National Football League (NFL) has said that prediction markets are "gambling" and not "swaps" as companies such as Kalshi and Polymarket claim. The professional football league made the statement in a brief it filed related to a case that's before the U.S. Supreme Court. The NFL is supporting the State of New Jersey in its assertion that prediction markets are gambling and should be regulated alongside casinos and other gaming companies.

Thailand Allows Trading In Crypto ETFs: Thailand is opening its main stock exchange to Bitcoin and Ethereum (CRYPTO: $ETH) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) starting on Oct. 16. Bitcoin and Ethereum will be the only cryptocurrency ETFs available on Thailand's stock market during the initial rollout. Each crypto ETF must operate as a passive investment fund designed to track the spot price of Bitcoin or Ethereum.

Stripe Expands Stablecoin Cards To 100 Countries: Financial technology company Stripe says it plans to expand its stablecoin payment cards to more than 100 countries by year's end. Stripe said the expansion is part of its bet that digital dollars can become another way for consumers and businesses to make payments alongside traditional currencies. Stablecoin cards have emerged as a fast-growing part of the $300 billion U.S. market for digital dollars. About $1.2 billion U.S. of stablecoins were spent through cards in September of this year, triple the amount from a year earlier, according to Paymentscan.

Winklevoss Twins To Launch New Zcash ETF: Twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss are planning to launch a new Zcash (CRYPTO: $ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The ETF will hold ZEC directly. The new ETF proposes charging a 0.25% annual fee and will be listed on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "WINK." The fund still needs to be approved by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Crypto Job Postings Tripled In September: Cryptocurrency companies are ramping up their hiring as prices for digital assets rally and the "crypto winter" that began a year ago shows signs of ending. Crypto firms listed 1,241 job openings in September compared to 886 in August and 382 in July, according to data from crypto recruitment platform CryptoJobsList. The September total was more than double the 573 jobs posted in January of this year, which was the busiest month of the year until August.

Coinbase Targets Banks: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase Global (NASDAQ: $COIN) is targeting banks as institutional adoption of cryptocurrencies continues to grow. Coinbase is expanding its services for banks and other traditional financial firms as institutions continue to adopt Bitcoin and other crypto. Coinbase and other crypto firms are offering services such as custody, trading, financing, and settlement to leading banks around the world.

title: Bitcoin holds ground above $82k, heads for weekly losses amid yield pressure
summary: Investing.com-- Bitcoin steadied above $82,000 on Friday and was set to snap a three-week gaining streak as concerns over rising yields and economic uncertainty pressured appetite for cryptocurrencies.
content:
Investing.com-- Bitcoin steadied above $82,000 on Friday and was set to snap a three-week gaining streak as concerns over rising yields and economic uncertainty pressured appetite for cryptocurrencies.

Before you buy NVIDIA: our AI model's stock picks are beating the market by 120%+. See the list now »

The world's biggest cryptoBitcoin edged up 0.7% to $82,391.3 by 16:39 ET (20:39 GMT), and was set to lose about 4.5% this week.

Broader crypto prices also fell on Friday and lagged Bitcoin for the week, as a strong third-quarter performance in the sector gave way to profit-taking through early-October.

Buying action by Strategy Inc (NASDAQ:MSTR) and more U.S. regulatory favor did little to limit Bitcoin's decline this week.

Bitcoin fell consistently this week as surging yields dented appetite for speculative, risk-driven assets. What little risk-on buying that did take place this week was directed largely towards artificial intelligence stocks, which drove Wall Street to record highs.

Crypto markets were seen losing their appeal amid growing confidence that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates at least once more before the year-end, as it grapples with sticky inflation.

A strong performance through the September quarter also opened up the sector to profit-taking, with traders now questioning whether the "uptober" trend of crypto gains in October will play out in 2026.

Not finding the right stocks? Our AI's list of investor-grade stock picks for October just dropped »

Bitcoin in particular was also pressured by renewed capital outflows from exchange-traded funds. Data from SoSoValue showed spot Bitcoin ETFs headed for their first weekly outflow in four, at over $700 million.

Surging oil prices also pressured crypto markets, although crude took a breather on Friday after U.S. President Donald Trump said there would be no new attacks on Iran until the November mid-term elections.

Broader crypto prices fell on Friday, with most major altcoins lagging Bitcoin for the week.

World no.2 crypto Ether edged 0.2% to $2,478.29 and was trading down over 8% this week.

XRP rose 0.6% meanwhile BNB edged 0.7% higher but it has lost over 7% this week.

Solana and Cardano fell 1% and 0.2%, respectively.

Among memecoins, Dogecoin and $TRUMP reversed course and were up 0.4% and 1.3%.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.
